description: Hand-written out-of-domain texts used to evaluate out-of-domain detection. Written by the project author for this evaluation; they are not real articles and are not drawn from any dataset. Genres deliberately differ from the WELFake training data (US political news, 2016-2017).

samples.text: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees Celsius and line a baking tray with parchment. In a large bowl, whisk together two cups of flour, one teaspoon of baking powder and a pinch of salt. In a separate bowl, cream the butter with the sugar until pale and fluffy, then beat in the eggs one at a time. Fold the dry ingredients into the wet mixture, adding a splash of milk if the dough feels stiff. Spoon tablespoons of dough onto the tray, leaving space between each, and bake for twelve minutes until the edges turn golden. Let the biscuits cool on a wire rack before serving with tea.

We investigate the thermal conductivity of silicon nanowires with diameters between 20 and 100 nanometres using a suspended micro-bridge measurement platform. Phonon boundary scattering dominates heat transport at room temperature, producing a conductivity roughly two orders of magnitude below that of bulk silicon. A modified Callaway model that includes diffuse surface scattering reproduces the measured temperature dependence between 50 and 300 kelvin. Our results indicate that surface roughness, rather than doping concentration, is the principal parameter controlling thermal transport in these structures, with implications for thermoelectric energy conversion.

The lighthouse keeper climbed the spiral stairs slowly, one hand on the cold iron rail, listening to the wind worry at the shutters. Below him the sea was black and restless. He had kept the lamp burning for thirty winters, and tonight, for the first time, he thought he heard someone knocking at the door at the bottom of the tower. He stopped on the landing and held his breath. The knocking came again, patient and soft, like a question. Somewhere out in the dark a bell began to ring, though there was no ship in the bay and no bell on the rocks.

To install the package, run the install command in your project directory and then import the client class in your application. Create a client instance by passing your API key and an optional timeout in seconds. The client exposes a get method that accepts a resource identifier and returns a parsed response object. If the request fails, the method raises a RequestError with the status code and a message. Use the retry option to enable exponential backoff for transient errors. Configuration values can also be provided through environment variables, which take precedence over defaults in the configuration file.

I bought this vacuum cleaner three months ago and I'm genuinely impressed. The suction is strong enough to pull dust out of the carpet, and the battery lasts about forty minutes on the standard setting, which is plenty for my two bedroom flat. The bin is easy to empty and the attachments click on securely. My only complaint is that it is a little heavy when used above head height. The filter needs rinsing once a month. Overall I would recommend it to anyone who wants a cordless model without paying premium prices. Four and a half stars.

The old town is best explored on foot, starting at the cathedral square where the morning market sells local cheese, honey and handmade ceramics. From there, follow the narrow lane past the clock tower to the river promenade, lined with cafes that serve strong coffee and almond pastries. Allow two hours for the castle museum, which has an excellent collection of medieval armour. In the evening, the terraces fill up with families and students, and many restaurants offer a fixed price menu. Trains to the coast leave every hour from the central station, and the journey takes about forty minutes.

A quadratic equation has the form ax squared plus bx plus c equals zero, where a is not zero. The solutions can be found by factoring, by completing the square, or by applying the quadratic formula. The discriminant, defined as b squared minus four ac, determines the number of real solutions: if it is positive there are two distinct real roots, if it is zero there is exactly one repeated root, and if it is negative there are no real roots but two complex conjugate roots. Graphically, the solutions correspond to the points where the parabola crosses the horizontal axis.

Revenue for the third quarter rose eight percent year over year to 4.2 billion dollars, driven by growth in the subscription segment and favourable currency movements. Operating margin improved by 120 basis points to 17.5 percent as the company reduced logistics costs. Net income was 610 million dollars, or 1.34 dollars per diluted share. Free cash flow totalled 780 million dollars. Management raised its full year guidance for revenue growth to between six and seven percent and reiterated its plan to repurchase up to one billion dollars of shares over the next twelve months.

Autumn arrives quietly, carried on the smell of woodsmoke and wet leaves. The orchard is heavy with late apples, and the grass beneath the trees is dotted with fallen fruit that wasps visit in the slow afternoon light. Swallows gather on the telephone wires, restless and talkative, rehearsing the long flight south. In the evenings the sky turns the colour of a ripe peach before darkening to violet, and the first cold stars appear above the barn roof. Everything seems to be letting go, gently, without any hurry or regret.

Photosynthesis is a biological process by which plants, algae and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy stored in organic compounds. In plants it takes place mainly in the chloroplasts of leaf cells, where the pigment chlorophyll absorbs light, chiefly in the blue and red parts of the spectrum. The overall reaction consumes carbon dioxide and water and releases oxygen. The process is usually divided into the light-dependent reactions, which produce adenosine triphosphate and reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate, and the Calvin cycle, which uses those products to fix carbon into sugars.

The city is situated on the northern bank of the river at the point where it widens into an estuary, and has a population of approximately four hundred thousand. Its economy historically depended on shipbuilding and the export of wool, and today relies chiefly on services, education and light manufacturing. The old quarter contains a Romanesque cathedral completed in the twelfth century and a medieval bridge with five arches. The climate is temperate maritime, with mild winters, cool summers and rainfall distributed throughout the year. The city is served by an international airport and a rail link to the capital.

Copper is a chemical element with the symbol Cu and atomic number 29. It is a soft, malleable and ductile metal with very high thermal and electrical conductivity, and a freshly exposed surface has a pinkish-orange colour. Copper occurs naturally as a native metal and in minerals such as chalcopyrite and malachite. It has been used by humans for more than ten thousand years, and alloys with tin produce bronze while alloys with zinc produce brass. Today it is widely used in electrical wiring, plumbing, roofing and coinage, and it is essential in trace amounts for most living organisms.

The common kingfisher is a small bird in the family Alcedinidae, found across Europe, Asia and North Africa. Adults have bright blue upperparts, orange underparts and a long, pointed bill, and typically measure sixteen centimetres in length. The species feeds mainly on small fish, which it catches by diving from a perch above the water. Pairs excavate nest burrows in riverbanks, and the female usually lays between six and seven white eggs. Populations are affected by water pollution and harsh winters, but the species is currently assessed as being of least concern.

The treaty, signed in the spring of that year, ended a conflict that had lasted nearly three decades and redrew the borders of several kingdoms in central Europe. Its terms recognised the sovereignty of the participating states, established a framework for religious toleration and required the withdrawal of foreign armies from the territories concerned. Historians generally regard the settlement as an important step in the development of the modern system of states, although debate continues about how far it genuinely altered the balance of power in the region in the decades that followed.

Rugby union is a contact team sport played between two teams of fifteen players using an oval ball on a rectangular grass field with H-shaped goalposts at each end. Points are scored by grounding the ball beyond the opposition's goal line for a try, and by kicking the ball between the posts for conversions, penalties and drop goals. Players advance the ball by running with it or kicking it, and may pass it only sideways or backwards. The sport originated in England in the early nineteenth century and is now played in more than one hundred countries.
